texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.Why Tempo?: Stablecoin payments are where my whole background converges. At Everex (Singapore) I wrote smart contracts and led government/bank relations across SE Asia on structuring crypto payments and stablecoins; at Platinum I designed one of the first detailed frameworks for a national government to issue its own stablecoins (regulatory + token-economic design) and shipped crypto-exchange infrastructure - backends, market-maker engines, high-frequency trading systems. Payments rails are adversarial by default, and I bring anti-fraud instincts from a decade in adversarial crypto markets plus an MSc in Computer & Information Systems Security (cryptography). Today I build guardrails for production AI agent fleets (agent-leash, verbatim-citation-gate) and run the attack surface I defend: a 6-machine Claude fleet operated in public. A payments-first chain needs product security from someone who has both audited the contracts and sat across the table from the banks and regulators who rely on them.
texts.Provide (2) examples of your exceptional: (1) I run the attack surface I defend: a production 6-machine Claude agent fleet operated in public, with published reliability evals - 0/17 high-risk (Tier-2) actions slipped past the human approval gate in recorded runs - plus open-source guardrails (agent-leash, verbatim-citation-gate, MIT). (2) I designed one of the first detailed frameworks for a national government to issue its own stablecoins (regulatory + token-economic design) and led government/bank relations across SE Asia on crypto payments at Everex - security work in maximally adversarial, compliance-heavy environments.
